data.title: What Goes in the Box
data.text:
I have put the boxes in order again. I am Mara Vey. I grew up below these valleys; the papers still have their old folds.

At Riverside, the water took empty No. 14 Church Lane, with its calendar, untuned piano and eleven boxes of this archive. I kept the piece of chalk. At Achadh, the green door still sticks. Mum says the pencil marks on the larder frame are all there. You left that farmhouse intact.

At the end, you broke the Upper Vell dam and the fjord chapel, but Tomas Lind’s chalet remained. His letter asks for a new stake line, higher up, where the ice still is. I have set it beside the old measurements.

Gil Harrow gave his reasons for the spillway being deferred in 2009 and again in 2016: the inspectors called the dam satisfactory, the harbour needed dredging, the school roof leaked, and he thought there was time. Those reasons sat together in his letter; the costs did not fall together.

Annex F, the second crossing at the Tobel, is approved, funded and scheduled at last. I keep the notice where I can find it. You cannot undo the river behind you. You can still decide where it goes next.
